source.title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems

accepted.question_text: Which infinite mathematical structures have a direct analogue of Ramsey's theorem? Here a direct analogue means that, for finite colorings of the relevant finite substructures of the infinite structure, one can find an isomorphic infinite substructure on which all those finite substructures are monochromatic, as happens for k-element subsets of the natural numbers and for k-uniform complete hypergraphs on infinitely many vertices.

evidence.quote: Theorem 1.1 (Ramsey, [58]). Given positive integers k and r and a coloring of the k-element subsets of the natural numbers N into r colors, there is an infinite set of natural numbers N ⊆ N such that all k-element subsets of N have the same color.
Question 1.2. Which infinite structures carry an analogue of Ramsey’s Theorem?

accepted.question_text: For which infinite structures S does every finite substructure A have a finite big Ramsey degree? Equivalently, for each finite A contained in S, is there a positive integer T such that every finite coloring of the copies of A in S admits an isomorphic subcopy S' of S in which the copies of A use at most T colors; when such T exists, the least possible T is the big Ramsey degree T(A).

evidence.quote: Question 1.3. For which infinite structures S is there a Ramsey-analogue in the following sense: Let A be a finite substructure of S. Is there a positive integer T such that for any coloring of the copies of A into finitely many colors, there is a subcopy S′ of S in which there are no more than T many colors for the copies of A?
The least such integer T , when it exists, is denoted T (A) and called the big Ramsey degree of A in S

accepted.question_text: What is the essential nature of a big Ramsey degree? In particular, when a Fraisse class K has the finite Ramsey property but its Fraisse limit usually does not have all big Ramsey degrees equal to one, what structural or combinatorial mechanism explains the unavoidable number of colors that must persist in every isomorphic copy of the limit structure?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2. What is a big Ramsey degree?

What is the essential nature of a big Ramsey degree? Why is it that given a Fraı̈ssé class K satisfying the Ramsey property, its Fraı̈ssé limit usually fails to carry the full analogue of Ramsey’s Theorem 1.1 (i.e. all big Ramsey degrees being one)?

accepted.question_text: Given a countably infinite homogeneous structure K, determine the full hierarchy of its big Ramsey theory: first, whether K has finite big Ramsey degrees for every finite substructure; second, if finite degrees exist, whether the exact degrees can be characterized by canonical partitions and then calculated or algorithmically computed; and third, whether K carries a big Ramsey structure, meaning an optimal finite expansion whose finite substructures have big Ramsey degree one with coherent unavoidable colorings.

evidence.quote: A structure K is homogeneous if each isomorphism between finite substructures of K extends to an automorphism of K.

Question 2.3. Given a homogeneous structure K, (1) Does K have finite big Ramsey degrees? That is, can one find upper bounds ensuring that big Ramsey degrees exist? (2) If K has finite big Ramsey degrees, is there a characterization of the exact big Ramsey degrees via canonical partitions? If yes, calculate or find an algorithm to calculate them. (3) Does K carry a big Ramsey structure?
A big Ramsey structure is essentially a finite expansion K∗ of K so that each finite substructure of K∗ has big Ramsey degree one

accepted.question_text: For which strong-amalgamation-property Fraisse classes K does the Fraisse limit of K have finite big Ramsey degrees? Here the strong amalgamation property means that when two finite structures are amalgamated over a common finite substructure, the two embedded copies intersect exactly in the embedded common part. In particular, decide whether finite big Ramsey degrees always exist for SAP Fraisse classes with finitely many relations and a finite set of forbidden substructures, whether they always exist for such classes when all relation arities are at most two, and find a general condition characterizing the SAP classes whose Fraisse limits have finite big Ramsey degrees.

evidence.quote: A Fraı̈ssé class K satisfies the strong amalgamation property (SAP) if given A, B, C ∈ K and embeddings e : A → B and f : A → C, there is some D ∈ K and embeddings e′ : B → D and f ′ : C → D such that e′ ◦ e = f ′ ◦ f , and e′ [B] ∩ f ′ [C] = e′ ◦ e[A] = f ′ ◦ f [A].
Problem 6.1. For which SAP Fraı̈ssé classes does the Fraı̈ssé limit have finite big Ramsey degrees?
Subquestions are the following: Given an SAP Fraı̈ssé class with finitely many relations and a finite set of forbidden substructures, does its Fraı̈ssé limit have finite big Ramsey degrees?

accepted.question_text: For big Ramsey degree results whose known proofs use forcing, find purely combinatorial proofs. The problem is especially open for k-clique-free homogeneous graphs with k at least 4 and for other relevant free-amalgamation-property classes, where the free amalgamation property is strong amalgamation with no additional relations beyond those inherited from the two structures being amalgamated.

evidence.quote: We say that K satisfies the free amalgamation property (FAP) if it satisfies the SAP and moreover, D can be chosen so that D has no additional relations other than those inherited from B and C.
Problem 6.2. For results whose proofs use the method of forcing, find new proofs which are purely combinatorial.
new methods will be needed for k-clique-free homogeneous graphs for k ≥ 4 and other such FAP classes.

accepted.question_text: Does every homogeneous structure that has finite big Ramsey degrees also carry a big Ramsey structure, and is there an exact correspondence between big Ramsey structures and topological dynamics analogous to the Kechris-Pestov-Todorcevic correspondence? The desired correspondence would give a dynamical understanding of big Ramsey degrees comparable to the known dynamical characterization for finite small Ramsey degrees.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.3. Does every homogeneous structure with finite big Ramsey degrees also carry a big Ramsey structure? Is there an exact correspondence, in the vein of the KPT-correspondence, between big Ramsey structures and topological dynamics?
The hope in Problem 6.3 is to obtain as complete a dynamical understanding of big Ramsey degrees as we have for small Ramsey degrees

accepted.question_text: Develop infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory on spaces of copies of a homogeneous structure. More concretely, extend the Galvin-Prikry and Ellentuck theorems from the Baire-space setting [omega]^omega to subspaces in which each infinite set represents a copy of a fixed homogeneous structure, ideally in a form that also recovers exact big Ramsey degrees.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.4. Develop infinite dimensional Ramsey theory on spaces of copies of a homogeneous structure.
The question in [41] asks for extensions of these theorems to subspaces of [ω]ω , where each infinite set represents a copy of some fixed homogeneous structure.
the infinite dimensional Ramsey theorem should ideally also recover exact big Ramsey degrees.

accepted.question_text: Develop big Ramsey degree theory for uncountable homogeneous structures, including the Ramsey theorems on trees of uncountable height needed to support such characterizations. Existing work characterizes examples such as the kappa-rationals and kappa-Rado graph under large-cardinal consistency assumptions, but the broader field for uncountable homogeneous structures remains open.

evidence.quote: The field of big Ramsey degrees for uncountable homogeneous structures is still quite open, but the fleshing out of the Ramsey theorems on trees of uncountable height has seen some recent work in [19], [20], and [68].
Džamonja, Larson, and Mitchell applied a slight modification of his theorem to characterize the big Ramsey degrees for the κ-rationals and the κ-Rado graph.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether reverse-mathematical strengths for big Ramsey structures differ for homogeneous structures whose big Ramsey degrees are not simply characterized, such as the triangle-free homogeneous graph or the generic partial order, compared with the rationals and the Rado graph.

evidence.quote: Computability-theoretic and reverse mathematical aspects have been investigated by Anglès d’Auriac, Cholak, Dzhafarov, Monin, and Patey.

As these structures both have simply characterized big Ramsey degrees, it will be interesting to see if different reverse mathematical strengths emerge for structures such as the triangle-free homogeneous graph or the generic partial order.
